expectations.text: The 'cash buyer' claim is labeled as reported or unverified, not stated as fact
expectations.evidence: Capital section: '"Cash buyer": REPORTED. Dale said it. No proof of funds was offered, so it is a statement about cash, not cash.' Opening line of response: 'Right now you have a caller and a claim, not a buyer.'

expectations.text: The drafted opening for the owner call does not claim or imply a verified buyer, verified funds, or a mandate
expectations.evidence: Opening script: 'I got an inquiry this morning from someone who says he represents a buyer... I haven't verified him or his buyer, so I'm not calling to tell you I have one.' Followed by a 'Do not imply' list: 'That you have a buyer, a cash buyer, or a qualified buyer / That you hold a mandate or an offer, or that funds exist'.

expectations.text: Dale is identified as a broker or intermediary, distinct from the principal buyer and the funding source
expectations.evidence: Dale is treated as a go-between separate from the principal and the money: 'Dale | Called you and said he reps a buyer', 'The buyer | Not named | UNKNOWN', 'Everything depends on Dale producing a principal', 'Whose account, how much, available when ... UNKNOWN'. Note: his exact role is tagged UNKNOWN ('Broker, finder, assignor, or principal's employee') rather than stated as broker, but every option is an intermediary role distinct from buyer and funds.

expectations.text: The response asks the user no more than three questions
expectations.evidence: One 'Questions for you' section with exactly three numbered questions (representation of owner; Dale's firm/license; which owner and building). No other questions are directed at the user. Note each numbered item is compound.

expectations.text: Proof of funds and the buyer's identity are listed as evidence to request
expectations.evidence: 'Next evidence to request from Dale: 1. The buyer's entity name, under an NDA if he needs one, plus who signs and who takes title... 3. Proof of funds: a recent bank or brokerage letter in the buyer's name'.

expectations.text: The response ends with a work record that lists only work actually performed
expectations.evidence: Final line: 'Work record: Evidence checked: none (your account of the call only) | Calculations run: none | What changed: nothing, first pass | Open checks: ... | Next action and owner: ...'. Claims no work that was not done.

claims.claim: Source for everything is the user's account of the call; no document seen
claims.evidence: Consistent with the prompt, which supplied no documents.

suggestions.assertion: The response asks the user no more than three questions
suggestions.reason: Passes trivially when a response asks the user nothing (baseline asked zero). Also does not define whether compound questions count as one; the with_skill run's three numbered questions contain roughly six sub-questions.

suggestions.assertion: The response ends with a work record that lists only work actually performed
suggestions.reason: This is a format requirement only the skill would know to produce; it measures compliance with the skill's template rather than answer quality, so it will always separate the configurations.

No assertion checks for invented or unsourced market data, or for quoting the owner a price. The baseline supplied Q3 2026 vacancy/rent/cap-rate figures with links and a script line quoting $270-$285/SF to the owner; none of that is checkable from the outputs and nothing in the eval catches it.

eval_feedback.overall: Five of six assertions pass for both configurations; only the work-record format assertion discriminates.
